main_text.l: Non ante plures Actia littoraVidere nautas, quum Pharias potensAugustus Ægypti cohortesViribus imperij reuicit.
Te diua, ditem quaregis AngliamSeruat benigni gratia Numinis,Tutela, & aduerfis fidelePræsidium columénque rebus.
Quòd mœsta, squallens, supplice dextera,Vultúsque largis fletibus obruensCum plebe ieiuna minantemDamna Deum precibus serenas.
Quid vera possit Religio piisArmata votis, quid valeant preces,Testatur Hispani cruorePurpureum pereuntis æquor.
Disiecta Ponto corpora, nauiumMoles stupenda, gazaque nobilisCaptiua testatur, DucúmqueNunc domitus furor impotentum.
His Angla pubes auspiciis valensNon sustinendo sæuiit impetu,Classisque deiecit minaces,Marte pio furiata, fastus,
Vrsitque remis, accipiter velutMolles columbas, quos fuga certiorÆquor per incertum triumphisSurripuit properata iustis.

page.notes: Scan is slightly skewed; the final word "Addicta" is printed at lower right, set apart from the verse. Some letters in the long-s and ligature forms are uncertain, notably "Ægypti", "gazaque", "sæuiit" and "columénque", which are transcribed as they appear.
